questions.question: Compare job production and flow production, giving one advantage and one disadvantage of each.
questions.correctAnswer: Job production advantages: unique, high-quality products that command premium prices; fully customised to customer needs. Disadvantages: slow, labour-intensive, high unit cost, difficult to scale. Flow production advantages: high output, low unit cost, consistent quality, economies of scale. Disadvantages: inflexible, high set-up costs, standardised products with no customisation, breakdowns halt

questions.question: Explain how lean production can reduce a business's costs.
questions.correctAnswer: Lean production reduces costs by: eliminating waste (overproduction, waiting time, defects, excess inventory), using JIT to reduce storage costs (stock arrives only when needed), kaizen for continuous small improvements that cumulatively reduce costs, and reducing rework/returns through quality focus. questions.question: Evaluate which production method a furniture maker should use if they want to expand from bespoke to selling online nationwide.
questions.correctAnswer: Currently using job production (bespoke). Expanding nationwide online requires: higher volume, consistent quality, lower unit costs. Batch production is the best intermediate step: can produce in batches for online orders while still offering some customisation. questions.correctAnswer: A grade 9 response will: analyse current batch production (quality, variety, flexibility, but limited volume); flow production benefits (high volume, low unit cost, consistent output for supermarket contracts); flow production drawbacks (loss of artisan quality, high capital investment, inflexibility, potential brand damage); alternatives (expand batch capacity, invest in semi-automated hybrid). Conclude: switching fully to flow risks damaging the brand's artisan image - a phased approach adding some automation while retaining craft methods for premium lines would be more prudent.
